def kth_xor_walk_cost(n, edges, s, t, k):
    """
    You are given an undirected multigraph on vertices 1..n (1 <= n <= 60).
    `edges` is a list of at most 200 triples (u, v, w) with 1 <= u, v <= n
    and integer weight 0 <= w < 2**30. Parallel edges and self-loops are
    allowed. Every edge may be traversed in either direction, any number of
    times.

    A walk from s to t is any sequence of consecutive edge traversals that
    starts at vertex s and ends at vertex t; the empty walk (allowed exactly
    when s == t) is a valid walk of cost 0. The cost of a walk is the
    bitwise XOR of the weights of all its traversals, where an edge used
    multiple times contributes once per traversal (so using an edge twice
    cancels its weight).

    Let C be the set of DISTINCT costs achievable over all walks from s to
    t (C is always finite). Given an integer k with 1 <= k <= 2**62, return
    the k-th smallest element of C (1-indexed). If no walk from s to t
    exists, or if k > len(C), return -1. The result is a single int; there
    are no ties because C contains distinct values.

    >>> kth_xor_walk_cost(3, [(1, 2, 1), (2, 3, 2), (1, 3, 4)], 1, 3, 1)
    3
    >>> kth_xor_walk_cost(4, [(1, 2, 1), (2, 3, 2), (3, 4, 4), (1, 3, 5), (2, 4, 8)], 1, 4, 3)
    9
    >>> kth_xor_walk_cost(2, [], 1, 2, 1)
    -1
    """
